ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors, representatives, and counterparties against the UIAF consolidated PEP list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Colombian domestic lists issued by the Consejo Nacional de Estupefacientes, and the Procuraduría General de la Nación ineligibility registers; enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons, high-risk jurisdictions, and irregular transaction patterns.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) – Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (www.rues.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory name reservation is processed in Spanish; a proposed name originally in another language or alphabet must be transliterated into the Spanish Latin script. The name must be unique within the commercial registry, must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name or well-known trademark, and must comply with the principles on corporate names under the Colombian Commercial Code and Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio guidelines.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición y en subsidio apelación' before the same Chamber of Commerce within ten (10) business days from notification, or submit a new alternative name after resolving the conflict. Appeals against the registry's final rejection are decided by the Superintendencia de Sociedades or the competent ministerial authority, as applicable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered agent address is permissible as the legal domicile of the S.A.S., provided that it includes a physical point capable of receiving statutory mail and service of process. A pure cloud-based SaaS developer with no local employees may use such an address, but must maintain a designated authorized agent for Colombian legal notifications and have adequate records demonstrating commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – less than 5% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk SaaS entity; tax and registry audits normally rely on documentary review and may require telephonic or digital evidence of substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas), Articles 4, 5, 8, 9, 17, 22 and 45; Código de Comercio (Decree 410 of 1971), Articles 110, 111, 354; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 of 2015, Book II on mercantile registration; Law 1429 of 2010 on company formalization.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or the Cámara de Comercio of the city of the registered office) acting as keeper of the Registro Mercantil; corporate supervision by the Superintendencia de Sociedades; fiscal registration by DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation deed under Article 5 of Law 1258 of 2008) filed for recording in the Registro Mercantil, together with the Formulario de Registro Único Tributario (RUT) and the resulting Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 1258 of 2008 imposes no minimum paid-up capital. The sole shareholder may subscribe capital with payment deferred up to 24 months (Article 8); no escrow account is mandated, but contributions must be paid into the company account and non-monetary technology contributions must be appraised under Article 9.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole incorporator of the S.A.S. approves the subscription of all one hundred thousand issued shares at par value COP 100 each, totaling COP 10,000,000, to be paid into the company account within 24 months as permitted by Law 1258 of 2008. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is established at Calle 93 No. 14-45, Office 601, Bogotá. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed General Legal Representative, [Name] as Deputy Representative, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Legal Representative is authorized to apply for the RUT, municipal registration, corporate bank account, and any government approvals for commencing the software analytics business. All prior acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Verification and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá online portal (Registro Mercantil virtual notice service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Chamber's virtual platform, submit a homonym search (consulta de homonimia) for the chosen corporate name, and obtain the certificate of name availability. The name is automatically reserved for 30 business days; complete the reservation before submission of the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Applicant ID document
Proposed corporate name
Activity description matching ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511
Digital application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is unavailable or confusingly similar, propose three alternative names and file a new reservation request without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Deed and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sole shareholder executing the Documento Privado de Constitución; notary required only if real property is contributed (not applicable here)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the private incorporation deed containing the by-laws, share subscription, corporate purpose for SEO/MarTech software services, legal representative appointment, and the precise ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511 scope. Sign electronically using a Cámara-certified digital signature platform or physically before the Chamber.
required_dossiers: ID documents of incorporators
Name reservation certificate
Draft by-laws (estatutos sociales) under Law 1258 of 2008
Capital contribution payment receipt (bank account) or appraisal report for IP contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber identifies formal defects, execute a corrigendum or rectification document embodying the observations and resubmit within the correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registration and Issuance of Existence Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation deed through the Chamber's online filing system, pay the registration tariff and the departmental impuesto de registro, and request the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal. Register the corporate books (share ledger and minutes book) and attach the pre-registered RUT from DIAN.
required_dossiers: Documento Privado de Constitución with connected signatures
Name reservation certificate
RUT pre-registration slip
Proof of payment of registration fee and impuesto de registro
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any query within 15 business days by filing additional information; errors in the certificate may be corrected by a request for correction to the Chamber with prior authorization from the legal representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: DIAN Tax Registration, NIT Issuance and Electronic Invoicing Enablement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - Sede Electrónica portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) registration in DIAN's online system using the certificate of existence, obtain the definitive NIT, and activate the facturación electrónica scheme with digital signature (firma electrónica) to support Stripe/Paddle invoicing flows for the SaaS business.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
By-laws and incorporation deed
Legal representative ID and digital signature credentials
Contact and address data of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or queries the RUT filing, file a rectification (actualización del RUT) with corrected data and, where needed, request technical assistance through DIAN's virtual chat or a fiscal representative appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda (municipal treasury), Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos, and social security administrators (EPS/ARL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Impuesto de Industria y Comercio (ICA) and avisos y tableros at the municipal treasury of the registered office, obtain the fire-safety clearance for the office, open a corporate bank account, and register employees with EPS, ARL and pension administrators if hiring begins.
required_dossiers: RUT and NIT certificate
Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Lease contract for the registered office
Fire-safety inspection (solicitud de visita de bomberos)
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For municipal tax penalties arising from late ICA registration, file the initial declaration and request exoneración de sanciones by proving good faith and payment within the voluntary term; for fire-safety deficiencies, remedy inspection observations and request a re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial license authority applies to ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511. Optional voluntary registration with MinTIC (Registro TIC) and with Minciencias for CTeI tax benefits is available for software and MarTech ventures.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - office-based SaaS and data analytics activity requires no factory or manufacturing permit. Mandatory fiscal registrations are ICA (Impuesto de Industria y Comercio) and municipal avisos y tableros, which are tax registrations, not operating licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and local environmental authority at the registered office (e.g., Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente de Bogotá)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based software/SEO analytics activity generates no industrial effluent or emissions; no EIA, environmental license or registration is required under Decreto Único Reglamentario 1076 of 2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial discharge. If operating an office or leased data closet: wastewater only to municipal sewer per RAS Title B; e-waste, batteries and IT equipment must be delivered to licensed collectors under Resolución 1672 of 2013; no VOC emission sources are present in pure SaaS serverless operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) for office occupancy, structural load and occupancy clearance from building management, installation of extinguishers and evacuation signage, compliance with NTC 2050 / RETIE electrical standards, and registration of the workplace under Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) per Decreto 1072 of 2015 if staff are hired in Colombia.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – portal: www.dian.gov.co, with taxpayer transactions through MUISCA and electronic invoicing systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) must be incorporated before a notary and registered with the competent Cámara de Comercio; DIAN then assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). The company must complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) online or at a DIAN service point, update the RUT with the ISIC 6201 business activity, and obtain the applicable electronic invoicing authorizations. Foreign shareholders may hold ownership without residency; foreign legal representatives require an appointed local agent for tax domicile notice purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no federal check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. The S.A.S. is a resident corporate taxpayer taxed at the entity level; no pass-through regime is available. Qualified taxpayers may elect the Simplified Taxation Regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación – SIMPLE) under Articles 903–916 of the Tax Code when statutory turnover thresholds and ownership conditions are met. Export-related zero rating for VAT is mandatory when statutory requirements are satisfied, not an elective regime. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under domestic anti-deferral and CFC rules to the extent provided by Colombian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover threshold for VAT registration in Colombia; any person carrying out taxable activities is obliged to register as a VAT responsible party from the start of operations. For eligible small taxpayers electing the SIMPLE regime, the statutory annual gross income ceiling applies; for 2025 this equivalent is set by law in UVT (unidad de valor tributario), with the applicable UVT value announced annually by DIAN.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT registered taxpayers must issue the factura electrónica de venta (FEV) through DIAN-authorised software or an authorised technology provider. The invoice must be transmitted in real time to DIAN's electronic invoicing clearance platform and must contain the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) for sales invoices and the CUDS (Código Único de Documento Soporte) for supporting documents. DIAN validates and sets the digital stamping; credit notes and debit notes must also be transmitted in the same electronic format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to goods exported from Colombia where actual customs export is evidenced and the exporter legally repatriates the foreign currency. For services, including SEO content analytics SaaS and software-related services, zero rating applies when the service is rendered by a Colombian tax resident or domiciled entity, the service is used exclusively outside Colombia by a non-resident customer, the contract and consideration reflect a genuine cross-border transaction, and the service is not economically linked to taxable activities within Colombia. The analysis under Article 481 of the Tax Code and regulatory guidelines must be documented in the company's transfer pricing and VAT files.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación (DEX) accepted by DIAN/VUCE for goods exports
Commercial invoice describing the service and contractual export nature
Export service certificate or the approved form evidencing cross-border service provision
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical exports
Inward Remittance Certificate / Declaración de Cambio issued by an authorised local bank proving receipt of foreign currency
Evidence of the foreign client's tax residence and exclusive foreign use of the software/analytics service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may retroactively disallow zero-rated treatment and claim VAT plus default interest when export documentation, foreign use evidence, or currency repatriation does not meet the statutory conditions. The taxable review period generally covers the last three to five tax years depending on the omission. Penalties include the inaccurate return penalty for omitted VAT, which may reach 100% or, in cases involving fraudulent supporting documents, up to 160% of the disputed amount. Criminal exposure may arise under Colombian anti-smuggling and tax fraud rules when false export declarations are used.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia); foreign-exchange policy is set by its Board of Directors (Junta Directiva) under Ley 9 de 1991, restated in Resolución Externa 1 de 2018 (compiling Resolución Externa 8 de 2000). The Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia authorizes and supervises the foreign-exchange intermediaries (IMCs/mercado cambiario) that execute compulsory exchange declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is fully convertible for current-account flows, including cross-border SaaS and software service exports, provided the payments are channeled through the Mercado Cambiario (MCR) via an authorized IMC and a Declaración de Cambio is filed. Capital account inflows and outflows are liberalized for registered foreign direct investment (FDI): equity contributions and intra-group loans become freely remittable once registered in Banco de la República's International Investment Registry (Registro de Inversores Internacionales) within 12 months of disbursement. Profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders is permitted after the 35% Colombian corporate income tax (2025 rate) and a 7.5% dividend withholding tax on the distributeable amount; an unregistered investment loses the FX right to remit dividends and capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For service exports within ISIC 6201 (SEO analytics SaaS), 100% of the foreign-currency proceeds must be channeled (canalizado) through the MCR and repatriated (reintegro) to an authorized IMC within 6 months from the invoice date, or from the contractual payment due date when such due date is later. The proceeds may be temporarily held in a foreign-currency account only during the pending reintegro window and must then be sold to or deposited with the IMC; statutory extensions are available if the exporter proves a documented collection delay by the foreign client. The export is declared electronically through the IMC using the service-concept code applicable to informatics and software services, and no prior regulatory license is required for the SaaS activity itself.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules_detail: The exporter must retain the underlying commercial contract, the foreign-currency invoice, the SWIFT credit advice, and the IMC-issued exchange declaration for five years. Offsetting eligible foreign costs (e.g., overseas cloud infrastructure) is strictly monitored; any netting must be pre-agreed in writing with the IMC and disclosed in the declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_restrictions: Foreign loans to the SAS with terms under one year are treated as short-term external debt and require annual registration with the Central Bank through the IMC; longer-term shareholder loans require debt registration to guarantee repayment through the MCR. Pure capital contributions (equity) do not require tax clearance but must be documented in the SAS bylaws amendment and reported to the Cámara de Comercio.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.dividend_repatriation_rules: Dividends declared by the SAS to its non-resident shareholder are remittable via the IMC after the 12-month FDI registration is effective; the bank will require the tax withholding certificate (form 2276) and the minutes of the shareholders' meeting approving the distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.reserve_requirements: No statutory reserve is required for minimum capital under Colombian SAS law, but banks may require the entity to maintain a liquidity buffer in a linked local account for fees and chargebacks on the Stripe and Paddle collections.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.future_regulatory_watchlist: Monitor Decree 1297/2022 on digital platforms and potential changes to the 7.5% dividend withholding for non-resident individuals; also track Superfinanciera Circular amendments on virtual onboarding standards which could allow remote KYC interviews within the next 12-24 months.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational COP account with MCR channeling plus USD clearing account; viable for capital escrow of shareholder contributions
Operational checking account and foreign-currency clearing account; robust FDI registration desk
Operational account with FX windows and foreign-currency current account; good digital corporates team
Operational account plus derivatives and hedging desk; suitable for NDF and forward structures
Operational account with standard MCR services
Operational account; good for USD-correspondent clearing but stricter onboarding timeline

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium as the primary treasury rail but Medium as a collection overlay. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Mercury, Airwallex, Payoneer) and payment aggregators (Stripe, Paddle) are not authorized Colombian IMCs; they cannot register FDI, file exchange declarations, or perform the statutory reintegro to Banco de la República. Their permissible role is limited to segregated collection/concentration of USD subscription receivables, with mandatory upstreaming to a Colombian IMC account within the 6-month reintegro window; longer retention requires a registered foreign-currency compensation account and triggers exchange-control and tax-reporting exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the legal representative or for a Colombia-resident attorney-in-fact holding a notarized, apostilled, and officially translated power of attorney. Bancolombia and Davivienda allow a remote pre-evaluation video call for low-risk corporate clients, but final account activation requires an in-branch interview and wet-ink signature of the SARLAFT forms; fully remote opening for a foreign-incorporated-managed SAS is not practically available. The natural person attending must present a Colombian cédula or cédula de extranjería and proof of address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder chain with no Colombian nexus and no documented source of funds; the ultimate beneficial owner is domiciled abroad with layered holding entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn declaration of source of funds, notarized proof of identification of the ultimate beneficial owner, corporate structure diagram, bank reference letter from the shareholder's home institution, and the DIAN Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) filing receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume low-ticket international collections through Stripe and Paddle inconsistent with the declared data-analytics business activity and possibly indicating payment card laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SaaS and licensing agreements, published pricing and product documentation, Stripe/Paddle payout reports covering at least 12 months, an updated client list, and a written AML business-risk self-assessment applying the simplified due diligence standard for low-risk digital exporters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident legal representative without Colombian tax presence and without local signing capacity, including inability of foreign directors to complete in-person police background checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled power of attorney appointing a Colombia-resident agent, certified copy of the foreign passport, proof of domicile abroad, legalized SAS incorporation documents, and a copy of the agent's cédula and RUT.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections arriving as equity or shareholder loans without prior Banco de la República registration, risking classification as suspicious flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-increase minutes, SWIFT credit advices, the electronic Declaración de Cambio for international investment, the 12-month FDI registration certificate, and the SARLAFT source-of-funds questionnaire completed at the IMC point of entry.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.onboarding_timeline_estimate: Standard onboarding for a foreign-owned low-risk SAS takes 4 to 8 weeks, including legalization of documents, background screening, and registry checks; expedited onboarding is possible at Bancolombia with complete digital dossiers and a local agent available for the interview.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.account_structure_recommendation: Maintain a primary COP operational account at Bancolombia for local payroll and vendor payments; establish a USD clearing account at the same bank to receive Stripe/Paddle payouts through the MCR; avoid opening multiple bank relationships in year one to simplify exchange declarations and FX reconciliations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders inject equity or subordinated debt via SWIFT MT103 in USD or EUR to the SAS's COP account at the IMC; the IMC applies the market exchange rate (TRM) and files the electronic Declaración de Cambio para Inversión Internacional Internacional, assigning a registration code. The SAS must record the investment in Banco de la República's International Investment Registry within 12 months of disbursement, supported by notarial capital-increase minutes, updated RUT, and the SARLAFT source-of-funds questionnaire; funds must not be fragmented or mislabeled to avoid reclassification as operating revenue. The IMC will require the beneficiary to present the tax identification (NIT) and the corporate existence certificate from the Cámara de Comercio upon credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For genuine cross-border disbursements (cloud hosting, data licensing, subcontractor fees), the SAS purchases FX through the IMC and remits via SWIFT MT103 using the appropriate SIREM concept codes for informatics, data processing, and software licensing. Open-account settlement with invoice matching will be the standard clearing method; commercial documentary credits (import/standby LCs) are structurally unnecessary for SaaS input procurement and are admissible only for large hardware or infrastructure contracts. All local operating expenditures (payroll, rent, Colombian vendors) remain in COP via ACH Colombia and the national payment system, minimizing FX conversion costs and leakage.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.collection_rail_integration: Stripe and Paddle settle USD/EUR balances to the Colombian IMC account via their banking partners; each payout is accompanied by a remittance detail that the bank maps to the FX declaration using the consolidated monthly payout report prepared by the CFO. To avoid per-transaction friction, the SAS should instruct Stripe and Paddle to batch daily payouts into one weekly settlement payment, and the treasury team must reconcile each settlement against the client-level report before the IMC closes the exchange declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_buffer_policy: Maintain an operating buffer of at least 45 days of fixed costs in COP; hold up to 15% of monthly SaaS collections as USD liquidity abroad for no longer than 20 days to cover vendor invoices before routing through the MCR; any USD funds held past the reintegro window are subject to Banco de la República penalties. Establish a monthly FX conversion calendar aligned with payroll and tax payment dates to reduce timing risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-COP spot and deliverable FX forwards executed solely through authorized IMCs (Bancolombia, Davivienda, or BBVA) with underlying commercial exposure
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the TRM, permissible for hedging the COP value of expected USD SaaS subscription receivables, with documentation of the forecast ticket and tenor

Cross-currency swaps combining COP and USD legs with IMC banks to manage long-term borrowed capital or intra-group financing, subject to Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia derivative limits and credit-line approval
OTC USD-COP FX options for collar or risk-reversal structures, with premiums and notionals aligned to the entity's actual export invoice pipeline
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.hedging_implementation_notes: All derivatives must be entered only after the board approves the hedging mandate and only with counterparties rated investment grade locally; NDF positions are typically settled in COP against the TRM, and the SAS must ensure the bank segregates the hedge P&L for tax reporting. No speculative FX positions are permitted; the treasury policy mandates that the notional of outstanding hedges never exceed 110% of forecast net USD inflows for the next six months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Annual Commercial Registration Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year between January 1 and March 31 inclusive; for a December 31 fiscal close, renewal due no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of approximately 3% of the renewal fee per month or fraction thereof plus mora interest; two consecutive years without renewal may trigger administrative strike-off, restriction on obtaining certificates, and legal standing loss.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Financial Statements and management report (Estados Financieros e Informe de Gestión)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than March 31 following the fiscal year-end, coinciding with the commercial registration renewal window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning and potential forced compliance order by Superintendencia de Sociedades, plus inability to validly file shareholder resolutions or debarment from the register until compliance is achieved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Corporate Income Tax Return, Form 110)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending December 31; due annually between July and September of subsequent year per DIAN calendar based on NIT last digit, of which SAS entities must comply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of the tax air per month (or fraction) capped at 100%, plus daily mora interest; update returns or delinquency can trigger extra penalties, asset embargos and suspension of tax operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Reporte Anual de Beneficiarios Finales (Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner – UBO Confirmation to DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually according to DIAN resolution; generally due on the same tax filing calendar and must be updated within 30 days of any shareholding or ultimate ownership transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial sanctions up to 4,000 UVT for omission or inaccurate information; late compliance may also bar shareholder registration and generate contingent tax risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit (Revisor Fiscal) is compulsory if gross assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.6 million in 2024) or if gross annual revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.0 million); also required when the shareholding structure or regulatory activity necessitates a permanent statutory auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NIIF para PYMES (IFRS for SMEs) as adopted by Colombia under Decreto 2420 of 2015, including the Financial Reporting Technical Framework for entity groups 2 and 3.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SAS entities must annually confirm the ultimate beneficial owner (‘beneficiario final’) dataset to DIAN within the designated tax window; any share transfer, dilution or change in control must be physically entered in the shareholder register and reported to DIAN as a UBO update within 30 days, otherwise the share transfer is inopposable and sanctionable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro de Registro de Accionistas (Register of Members)
Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas (Shareholder Minutes Book)
Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva (Board Minutes Book, if a board is constituted)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – 800 per year for virtual office or registered agent address
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – 7,000 for outsourced accounting and tax preparation; USD 8,000 – 20,000 for a full Revisor Fiscal if statutory threshold is exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (general CIT rate, Article 240 E.T., as maintained by Law 2277 of 2022 for fiscal years 2023 onward; financial sector surcharge of 3 percentage points applies only to credit institutions)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Economía Naranja (Orange/Creative Economy) exemption: 100% CIT exemption for the first 5 tax years and 50% exemption for the following 2 years for software developers classified under ISIC 6201-6202, conditioned on MinTIC/MinCultura certification, creation of at least 3 new direct jobs, investment of at least 1,300 UVT (COP 61,184,500 in 2024) in productive fixed assets, registration before 31 December 2025, and a timeline of 7 consecutive years. Export of digital/SaaS services is subject to 0% VAT and treated as export income; income from services rendered to non-residents for exclusive use abroad may be treated as foreign-source. No partial deemed-deduction regimes available to this ISIC scope.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry; Article 147 E.T. permits indefinite carryforward of net operating losses, indexed for inflation from the third year onward)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para Personas Jurídicas; filed mandatorily via the DIAN MUISCA electronic portal (www.dian.gov.co / muisca.dian.gov.co) using authorized e-agent credentials; supplementary forms in the same portal: Form 350 (VAT), Form 368 (advance payments), Form 2284/2285/2286 (transfer pricing), and exogenous information Form 2276 (dividend WHT report).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 110); advance income tax (anticipo de renta) paid within the annual filing window; bimonthly VAT returns; monthly payroll withholding and self-withholding returns; annual transfer pricing information returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual income tax return for the fiscal year ending 31 December is due between early April and mid-May of the following year, with the exact deadline determined by the final two digits of the NIT (tax ID). For a NIT ending in '23' (payload composite key), the 2025 filing window for tax year 2024 typically falls on 8–12 May 2025; the DIAN publishes the definitive calendar by resolution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos brutos totales (total gross income from all sources, including SAS SaaS subscriptions, SEO analytics licence revenue, and any foreign-source income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. is a Colombian tax resident and reports worldwide income; foreign non-resident shareholders do not file Form 110 for the S.A.S. If a non-resident permanent establishment exists, its allocable income is reported separately. Export income from services used exclusively abroad may be excluded as foreign-source under Article 24 E.T. only with full documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos (cost of sales including cloud infrastructure, data feed subscriptions) and deducciones (deductible operating expenses: payroll, marketing, subcontracting, depreciation of equipment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions require valid electronic invoicing (factura electrónica), contractual records, and actual banking flows via Stripe/Paddle reconciliation; disproportionate intercompany charges must satisfy arm's-length tests and can be disallowed if invoices from related non-residents lack withholding evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta líquida del ejercicio and rentas exentas (exempt income claimed under the Economía Naranja benefits for software/ISIC 6201 activities).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A qualifying S.A.S. must annex the MinTIC/MinCultura creative-industry certification and evidence of the 3-job and 1,300-UVT investment conditions; failure to support the exemption results in a 100%–200% inexactitude penalty. Non-resident shareholders cannot claim this exemption on dividend distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta líquida gravable (taxable income after exemptions), basic income tax at 35% (Renglón 50), and prior-year losses/advance payments (renglón 53).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable income must be computed on the accrual basis; losses of prior years offset without time limit but must be supported by the prior Form 110; non-resident shareholders have no input in this computation unless the S.A.S. has foreign shareholders' loans subject to thin-cap rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retenciones en la fuente practicadas al contribuyente (foreign tax credits and Colombian withholdings suffered) and saldo a pagar o a favor (final tax payable or refund).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits on payments received from abroad are claimable under Article 254 E.T. (capped at the Colombian CIT on the same income); any refund is offset against the S.A.S. tax liabilities before disbursement to non-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax; if no tax is payable, a flat penalty of 0.5% of gross income or net equity, capped by current UVT rules. Late payment interest: the DIAN applies the Bank of the Republic's monthly lending rate (approximately 1.5% per month, Article 635 E.T.). Additional sanction for filing without supporting e-invoicing: up to 2% of the invoice value in violation; failure to file the annual return at all triggers an 'official determination' with a 10,000-UVT sanction and criminal exposure for the legal representative.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid to non-resident shareholders: (i) 35% income tax on the portion of the dividend that corresponds to profits not previously taxed at the corporate level (i.e., exempt or specially taxed profits); and (ii) 10% withholding tax on the portion distributed from profits that have already borne 35% CIT. Combined effective burden on pre-tax earnings is approximately 41.5%. Statutory rate applies unless a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) reduces the 10% component, typically to 5%–15% for qualifying substantial shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief (e.g., Colombia–United States Treaty of 2012, Spain, Canada, Mexico, Chile, South Korea, UK, France, Switzerland), the non-resident shareholder must: (1) secure a Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) / Form 6166 from its home tax authority, (2) deliver the TRC and a sworn beneficial-ownership declaration to the S.A.S. before the dividend payment is made or within the same filing period, (3) have the S.A.S. record the reduced rate in the dividend minutes and in the exogenous information report to DIAN, and (4) retain TRC and LOB evidence for five years. If the TRC is not timely presented, the 35%/10% statutory rates are withheld at source and a refund must be pursued before DIAN, which in practice requires a two-year formal refund claim and full economic-substance documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical services: 15% statutory withholding (Article 408 E.T.); DTA rates commonly 10%–15% (US–Colombia: 15%; Canada, Spain, Mexico: 10% for copyright-related IP including software licences). Software licence fees paid by the S.A.S. to a foreign related licensor are subject to 15% WHT unless the licence is a genuine sale of software with a permanent transfer of the economic rights. Interest on cross-border debt: 15% statutory WHT; 5% reduced rate only for interest paid to foreign financial institutions registered with the Colombian Financial Superintendency; interest paid to related parties in excess of the 35%-EBITDA thin-cap limit is non-deductible and, if paid to a jurisdiction listed as non-cooperative, triggers a 35% WHT and full disallowance unless economic substance of the lender is proven.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For tax year 2024 (UVT = COP 47,065), mandatory documentation thresholds are: Local File (Información Local) – gross income above COP 6,118,450,000 (130,000 UVT), or gross assets above COP 5,177,150,000 (110,000 UVT), or net equity above COP 4,706,500,000 (100,000 UVT); Master File (Información Maestra) – the Colombian taxpayer has gross income above COP 7,530,400,000 (160,000 UVT) and belongs to a consolidated group with total joint income above COP 11,766,250,000 (250,000 UVT); per-counterparty transaction report (Form 2284) – when transactions with each foreign related party exceed COP 2,118,000,000 (45,000 UVT) per type. Even below these thresholds, all intra-group services, licence fees and SaaS cost-sharing arrangements must be supported by contemporaneous economic substance evidence.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not operate a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but a functional equivalent exists through: Article 869 E.T. general anti-abuse rule requiring legitimate business purpose; Article 260-1 E.T. arm's-length rule; CFC rules (Articles 882–886 E.T.); DTA beneficial-ownership conditions; mandatory Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales); and DIAN Circular 000014/2020 on transactions with non-residents. A Colombian S.A.S. attracting software development revenue with only a registered address, no payroll, no management meetings in Colombia, and no technical staff will be treated as a shell; DIAN may disregard its existence, reattribute the SaaS income to the non-resident principal, and levy the 35%/10% dividend/deemed-distribution WHT plus a 100%–200% inexactitude penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting revenue from Stripe and Paddle inflows, filing a false Form 110, destroying accounting records, or improper claim of the Economía Naranja exemption without certified qualifying activities, causing a tax underpayment exceeding 250 monthly minimum wages (approximately COP 347 million in 2024).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 4 to 9 years under Article 434-A of the Criminal Code; fines equal to 100% of the evaded tax; monthly interest under Article 635; late-filing penalty of 5% per month capped at 100%; asset seizure and mandatory filing of corrected returns. DIAN may also impose a 200% penalty when the false claim relates to exempt income (rentas exentas) without legal support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and controlling directors are jointly and severally liable under Article 793 E.T. for the unpaid tax and criminal fines; the DIAN may request travel bans (impedimento de salida del país) and preventive embargoes on personal assets pending fraud investigation; criminal liability attaches to the administrator who signs the false return.
